# Disagreement Log — T12_008 (Testament of Naphtali)
**Chapter:** T12_008 | **Verses:** 6 sections (~10 verses)
**Translators compared:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Arbiter:** SOPHIA

| # | Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA ruling |
|---|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|---------------|
| 1 | 3:1 | Body-parts catalogue | Full list | Full list | Summary: "the five senses in the head...spine for fortitude" | Full list retained — this is a unique physiological-theological taxonomy; compression loses its encyclopedic character |
| 2 | 5:2–3 | Vision content | Twelve stags, then Lamb vision | Extended: adds Mount of Olives vision and dream of bull | Twelve deer, then Lamb vision | EMET/PNEUMA version ("twelve deer") followed; LOGOS's extended dream material may be from a variant MS tradition |
| 3 | 5:3 | "Stags" vs. "deer" | "twelve-stags" | "twelve deer" | "twelve deer" | "twelve deer" — LOGOS/PNEUMA; the Greek elaphoi is gender-neutral |
| 4 | 6:2 | Death description | "he-covered-his-face-and-died" | "he covered his face and died" | "he covered his face — and died" | "he covered his face and died" — this striking image preserved; all three agree |
| 5 | Body-spirit parallel | Theological emphasis | Explicit chapter-verse structure | Expanded with "fitting every work of the Most High" | Simplified to "body is mirror of spirit" | SOPHIA retains core statement without LOGOS expansion; PNEUMA's "mirror" metaphor is elegant but not in MS |

---
*SOPHIA notes: Testament of Naphtali is unique in its protoscientific body catalogue (section 3) — the only passage in the Testaments where the physical body is mapped to psychological/spiritual faculties. The Lamb vision (5:3–4) is another Christian insertion universally flagged; SOPHIA retains without comment as it is in the MS. The death scene — "he covered his face and died" while still at table — is one of the most vivid death descriptions in the corpus.*
